title: In the future, do you think everyone will be both the developer and the end user?
author: PrettyPicturesNotTxt
selftext: When the tools become good enough, it would not be possible to try and hide the development process, as this can be easily reproduced from just the outputs alone. In effect, there will no longer be any "parasitic middle men" to stand in between creation and consumption, creation and development will be open to everyone, and the consumer will double as the creator.

comments.author: Vindelator
comments.body:
No. Not in game development.

AI can't generate a good creative vision for a AAA game. And that vision can't be polished and refined without human players. An AI can't *have* fun and that sort of thing isn't purely technical. Good games take real work and thought even if the code and art are generated. Basically, it can make a game exist, but it can't tell if it's good.

But for little things like an app to convert a file or something to organize a little task... that's the place where the end user can be the dev.

For example, I made a tiny utility that copies text to the clipboard from a screenshot. That's easy enough for anyone to make for themselves... or it will be when the tools get slightly more user friendly.

replies.author: _Dingaloo
replies.body: one thing I'm particularly excited for that is already basically here is that an end user can *mod* just about any game. At least mods that don't require new assets.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body:
Creation and in this case game development is a significant time investment and that alone already will stop people from doing it before we even get into other factors. Majority will just want to be entertained without having to work for it.

Thats if i got your question right lol

replies.author: PrettyPicturesNotTxt
replies.body:
> Creation and in this case game development is a significant time investment and that alone already will stop people from doing it before we even get into other factors.

At least when it comes to the time investment part, I think it will then just be a matter of throwing agent after agent at the project until it's done, which will be done mostly hands off. Of course, this will instead just shift the problem to who has the most money instead of who has the most time.

But even if people aren't inclined to do the full creation process from start to finish, I think plenty will be happy to remix existing works together in one giant pot and modify aspects that they do not like. We're already beginning to see some of that today.

replies.author: Vindelator
replies.body:
Unless there's some kinda shift in AI, one shot generated games are going to feel pretty hallow. Like a rerun of a show you've already seen. (Maybe something fundamentally will change but there needs to be a leap in creativity and subjective judgement of the human experience of a game.)

Modding games though or adding another level or a map might actually work pretty well. The AI would have a baseline of what's good and it could make something else with those rules.

comments.body: I think there will be platforms to make it easier for the average person but they might not have a huge amount of users. The average person still can’t navigate a file system with a GUI and has no interest in learning.

comments.author: Honest_Accident_8348
comments.body: As much as I hate this movie (never read the book), i see the future similar Ready Player One concept.  Where a game environment is more defined by “laws of the game universe” and the players create their own realities within those laws with prompts, vs a pre-programmed environment.  As ai gets more advanced, I think we will start to see trends like this.

comments.author: lorean_victor
comments.body: I don’t think it’ll happen for games in the traditional sense, as a lot of the work they require isn’t the technical aspects (coding / art / etc). but I do think surely for mini games or little interactive experiences. similar to how tiktok didn’t turn everyone into a movie director but resulted in lots more people becoming video creators.

comments.author: mrwolf214
comments.body: Things will look so different in 5 years we probably can't even imagine.  But that being said it will probably go one of two ways.  1) tell AI some stuff and have an instant game that works better than you can imagine today. True one prompt creation.  or 2) what I consider way more likely, the AI companies will price regular people out of the ability to use AI and it will only be something used by the wealthy and corporations.  And we'll be talking about those all too brief days in the latter half of the 2020s when we all got to use AI to make fun stuff.

replies.author: PrettyPicturesNotTxt
replies.body: I mean, I believe those in power are actually incentivized to make it as inexpensive as possible, since the would love a situation where "intelligence becomes so cheap that only the rich will think for themselves."

replies.author: mrwolf214
replies.body: I'd love it if that were true but this stuff is expensive and they can't depend on us poors to fund it.  They need way more money than we can provide to keep this gravy train rolling.

comments.author: sabertoothedhand
comments.body:
I'm not sure so I'll ask another question: is the trend towards user-generated content already treading this path? Will things really change that much if it is? 

Platforms like Roblox already exist entirely around purchaseable user-generated content, and for years games have come with baked-in level editors. Many games can just slap that stuff into the main game, like all the survival crafting games or Fallout 4's settlement system. 

Kinda seems to me like games will just start tacking on more user defined content that'll be less jank, like talking to an NPC for a bespoke armor set. Excited for if anyone manages to make it engaging for an Immersive Sim game, especially since the genre is dead as a doornail rn.

comments.author: I_Study_The_Patterns
comments.body: In the future do you think people will stop going to restaurants because they have a microwave at home?

replies.author: Feline_Fan
replies.body:
If the food you could get at home was exactly the same at the exact price point there would be no need to go to restaurants at all.  

My local supermarket has MUCH BETTER meals that they make and cook themselves for 5$-7$ a piece that you just put in your microwave than a fancy restaurant that I went to for a few family occasions that sell meals at $22 a pop.

There is NO NEED for restaurants at all if you can get the same of better food at home.

replies.author: cheyumaama
replies.body: People go to restaurants for vibe, variety and a particular taste that supermarket meals don't have. So for games, people would still spend money on high quality AAA style games, just not sloppy games that they can make themselves with a little prompting

comments.author: sumdeadhorse
comments.body: Nope, anyone can write a book but most readers don't

comments.author: CromagnonV
comments.body:
The only reason we have operating systems is to provide a graphical interface and representative view of what the computer is doing. If we're just talking to agents, then the os just becomes the agents screen. It can build is an interface for whatever app we want already. The only blocker currently is the hooks into the existing human centric front-end for banking, government website, etc that we generally don't want bundled into a data model. 

I'll go you one further, once the brain chips start rolling out and we figure out how to project directly into optic nerves and the central nervous system. Then we won't even need screens either. 

Then what even is subjective reality, the answer is unequivocally whatever we want it to be.
